native_result.query: What is the average length of original papers in Experimental Economics and that in Psychology?
native_result.HypoA: Studies in Experimental Economics tend to have longer original papers compared to Psychology. The average length of original papers in Experimental Economics is 28 pages, whereas in Psychology, the average is 11 pages.
native_result.HypoB: Using original-paper page counts (length) in the replication study file, original papers differ substantially by group. Experimental Economics (project='ee', the Experimental Economics Replication Project; n=18 original papers) averages 28.0 pages (median 27.5, sd 7.4, range 16-45). Psychology (project='rpp', the Reproducibility Project: Psychology; n=97 replication rows = 95 unique original papers) averages 11.2 pages (median 9.0, sd 6.3, range 1-31). So Experimental Economics original papers are on average ~16.8 pages longer than Psychology (RPP) original papers. Group labels use the project column because discipline has no 'Psychology' value, and project='ee' coincides exactly with discipline='Economics'; Many Labs (ml1/ml3) projects are excluded as separately labelled projects. The result is insensitive to row-vs-paper counting (97 vs 95) and to excluding the 7 rpp rows flagged drop=True (mean 11.0).
native_result.WorkflowB: Loaded main study CSV; verified length has no missing values (927/927) and defined groups via the project column (ee=Experimental Economics, 18 rows=18 papers; rpp=Psychology/RPP, 97 rows=95 unique papers) after confirming discipline has no 'Psychology' value and that project='ee' coincides exactly with discipline='Economics'. Computed per-group mean, median, sd, min, max at row level with unique-paper n as robustness, plus a sensitivity line excluding the 7 rpp rows flagged drop=True. Excluded Many Labs (ml1/ml3) projects per schema labels; aggregated column is NaN for both target groups; the second CSV has no length column and was excluded.
